content.overview: BNS s. 162 — Abetment of such assault, if assault committed.
content.study:
Introduction and meaning
Abetment of such assault, if assault committed. BNS restatement of IPC 134. Elements are substantially the same; cite the BNS number for offences on or after 1 July 2024. BNS restatement of IPC 134. Cite the BNS number for facts on or after 1 July 2024.
In student language: BNS s. 162 is the rule on “Abetment of such assault, if assault committed”. The section provides that whoever abets an assault by an officer, soldier, sailor or airman, in the Army, Navy or Air Force of the Government of India, on any superior officer being in the execution of his office, shall, if such assault be committed in consequence of that abetment be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years, and shall also be liable to fine. Do not stop at the heading. An examiner awards marks for the ingredients, the explanations and the illustrations, not for writing the title alone.

Why this is asked
Criminal law arguments turn on statutory ingredients. BNS s. 162 exists so that “Abetment of such assault, if assault committed” has a closed legal test in Chapter VIII — Of Offences Relating to the Army, Navy and Air Force. An authoritative analysis defines the concept, lists every ingredient, walks the statutory illustrations, states exceptions, and applies the test methodically to facts.
Chapter setting: Mutiny, desertion, insubordination, and wearing a service garb.
